content.text:
I'm figuring out the task: output should crop the bounding box of the object with a unique color, zeroing out other colors. I'm sketching a demo grid with repeated 3x3 color-4 boxes and one distinct larger box to illustrate the pattern.

I'm also planning a second demo with different shapes and colors to test the same rule further, working out the grid layout row by row.

Finishing the grid layout, I'm sketching the two small corner boxes and blank rows. I'm now considering a third demo variant, deciding to swap out the overlap idea for a diamond shape instead, and settling on two main demos (A and B) plus a diamond-based demo C on an 11x11 grid.

Working out the diamond's geometry, I'm placing color 5 cells at exact distance-3 offsets from center (4,5) to form the outer diamond shape, then figuring out where to position smaller radius-1 diamonds in color 1 -- one nested at the big diamond's center and others in corners -- making sure none of them touch the big diamond's border.
